llm.summary: The skill's code, instructions, and requirements are consistent with a local customer-service reply/template generator; it runs locally and writes modest data files, with no network exfiltration or unrelated credential requests detected.

llm.guidance: This skill appears coherent and local-only: it generates reply templates and stores logs/data under a user data directory (default ~/.local/share/customer-service-reply). Recommended precautions before installing: (1) open SKILL.md and the scripts in a text editor to confirm there are no hidden/obfuscated lines (the scanner flagged Unicode control characters), (2) if you don't want local logs, create a directory and set CUSTOMER_SERVICE_REPLY_DIR to a sandbox location or remove/inspect logging lines in scripts/script.sh, (3) run the scripts in a restricted environment the first time (or inspect the code) to verify behavior, and (4) be cautious if you see any unexpected network calls or credential requests — none are present in the included files.
llm.findings: [unicode-control-chars] unexpected: The pre-scan detected Unicode control characters in SKILL.md. These characters can be used for prompt-injection or to hide content, which is not needed for a template generator. The rest of the files appear readable and coherent, but you may want to inspect SKILL.md in a plain-text editor that reveals control characters before installing.
